You have Atlassian MCP tools available but DEFERRED. First run ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page" and max_results 2 to load the schema.

Then read these two Confluence pages IN FULL (convert_to_markdown=true, include_metadata=true):
1. Page ID 302776322 — "04.1.8 Product, Catalogue and PDP" (Req ID prefix PRD)
2. Page ID 303661057 — "04.1.9 Search and Recommendations" (Req ID prefix SPR)

Context: I am researching a "Recently Viewed products" feature (Jira SFCC-83 / SFCC-84) that stores a shopper's product browsing history — session-only for guests, account-persisted for logged-in shoppers — on the Zimmermann SFCC PWA storefront. I need the functional requirement(s) behind it AND the consent position.

For EACH page report:
- The page's version number (from metadata) and any "last updated" / "extracted on" date stated in the body text.
- EVERY requirement row mentioning "Recently Viewed", "recently viewed", browsing history, or a product-history carousel — quote the Req ID and full requirement text VERBATIM, plus its Owner / Storefront / Config-Custom / Status / Comments / User Story Link column values. Note if the row is struck through (out of scope).
- EVERY requirement row relating to consent, cookies, Didomi, privacy, tracking, or personalisation (e.g. Einstein recommendations, Measmerize) — quote verbatim with the same columns.
- Explicitly state whether either page states any DATA RETENTION PERIOD for browsing/personal data, and whether either distinguishes guest vs logged-in/authenticated storage or treatment.
- Note any per-region differences (AU vs EU/UK vs US vs HK/ME).

Quote verbatim; do not paraphrase requirement wording. If "Recently Viewed" does not appear at all on a page, say so explicitly and clearly. Do NOT modify anything — read-only. Do not write any files. Return findings as your final message.

Also in the body header: "⚠️ **Rows with strikethrough are out of scope** — struck through in the Excel source file."

# Cross-page synthesis for SFCC-83 / SFCC-84

**Two requirements back Recently Viewed, and they do not agree.** Both are Confirmed, both Accenture, both ALL, both Custom, both from the same 3 July 2026 extract:

| | PRD-027 (page 1) | SPR-61 (page 2) |
|---|---|---|
| Surfaces | PDP only | **PDP and Cart page** |
| Storage | "browsing **session** history" — session only | "browser session" **+ "persisted cross-session on login"** |
| UI | "carousel", overridden by Comments to a **"See full history"** button | "display … products" — no UI form stated, no See-full-history mention |

SPR-61 is the stronger requirement on every axis and is the one that matches the SFCC-83/84 framing (session for guests, account-persisted on login). PRD-027 adds the "See full history" surface that SPR-61 omits. Neither is struck through, so both are in scope and the delta is unresolved — worth flagging before build rather than picking one.

**The consent position is: neither page states one.** Across both pages there is no mention of Didomi, cookies, tracking consent, GDPR, or a privacy requirement of any kind. The only consent requirement anywhere in the two pages is **PRD-045**, which is marketing opt-in for the stock-alert form, gated by **Omneo** (not Didomi), and it does not touch browsing history. SPR-61 mandates storing and cross-session persisting a shopper's browsing history with **no consent gate, no storage mechanism, no retention period, and no regional variation** stated. That is a genuine gap in these two pages, not something I overlooked — the consent position for Recently Viewed will have to come from the Didomi/consent PRD or `.docs/prd/regional.md`, not from PRD or SPR.

**No data retention period is stated on either page**, for browsing history or for any other personal data (including the name/email captured by PRD-044).

**No per-region differentiation exists for anything in this feature area.** Page 2 is uniformly `ALL`; page 1's single region-scoped row (PRD-009, EN-EU/FR-EU) is AGEC environmental labelling, unrelated to privacy. Given the EU/UK opt-in-before-storage posture the project applies elsewhere, the absence of any AU-vs-EU split on SPR-61 is a likely omission rather than a deliberate "same everywhere" decision — but the pages do not say so either way.
